issues.legal_issue: The transitional provisions make the additional acquisition benefit available for land-acquisition proceedings commenced after the applicable transition boundary, whether or not the Collector had already made an award before the amending law commenced.
material_facts: The acquisition proceeding began after the transition boundary identified in the transitional provision.
The Collector made the award before the amending law commenced.
The landowners sought enhanced compensation in a reference proceeding.
issues.conclusion: The landowners were entitled to the additional benefit provided by Section 23(1A) of the Land Acquisition Act, 1894.
issues.legal_principle: Section 23(1A), read together with Section 30(1)(b) of the Land Acquisition (Amendment) Act, 1984, applies to acquisition proceedings commenced after 30 April 1982, whether or not the Collector made an award before the amending Act commenced. The Constitution Bench majority in K.S. Paripoornan v. State of Kerala construed these provisions together; Prem Chand v. Union of India applied that interpretation.

predicates.land_acquisition_proceeding: The proceeding was for the acquisition of land.
predicates.acquisition_started_after_transition_bou: The acquisition proceeding began after the applicable transitional boundary.

issues.definition: When a land-acquisition proceeding began after the transitional boundary, the landowner is entitled to the additional acquisition benefit.

issues.legal_issue: An appellate court may grant an otherwise lawful statutory benefit through its broad power to do complete justice even when the claimant did not file an independent appeal or cross-objection.
material_facts: The State appealed against the reference court's compensation award.
The landowners did not file an appeal or cross-objection but applied to the High Court under Order 41 Rule 33 of the Code of Civil Procedure for the additional benefit.
The landowners were legally entitled to the benefit under the applicable acquisition law.
No legal prohibition barred the appellate court from granting the requested benefit.
issues.conclusion: The High Court could grant the landowners the additional benefit under Order 41 Rule 33 despite their not having filed an appeal or cross-objection; its refusal of that relief was set aside to that extent.
issues.legal_principle: Order 41 Rule 33 of the Code of Civil Procedure gives an appellate court broad power to make the order required by the justice of the case and to do complete justice, subject to legal interdicts and the limitations described in Vanarsi v. Ramphal. Samundra Devi v. Narendra Kaur confirms that the power cannot override a legal interdict. The entitlement recognized in K.S. Paripoornan v. State of Kerala was binding under Article 141 of the Constitution.

rule.if: appellate_review_of_compensation_award and claimant_sought_benefit_in_appellate_court and claimant_filed_no_independent_appeal_or_cross_objection and acquisition_met_benefit_eligibility_conditions and no_legal_bar_to_relief

predicates.appellate_review_of_compensation_award: A compensation award was under appellate review.
predicates.claimant_sought_benefit_in_appellate_cou: The claimant applied to the appellate court for the benefit.
predicates.claimant_filed_no_independent_appeal_or_: The claimant filed neither an independent appeal nor a cross-objection.
predicates.acquisition_met_benefit_eligibility_cond: The acquisition satisfied the conditions that made the claimant eligible for the benefit.
predicates.no_legal_bar_to_relief: No legal prohibition prevented the court from granting the requested relief.

issues.definition: When a compensation award is under appellate review, the claimant seeks the benefit in that court without an independent appeal or cross-objection, the acquisition satisfies the benefit's eligibility conditions, and no legal bar applies, the appellate court may grant the requested benefit.
